extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, proofreaders, copyholders, and typesetting/production staff in book/journal publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Practical rules and conventions for preparing manuscripts, formatting heads/paragraphs, preparing and marking proofs, and for the work of proofreaders and copyholders in book and journal production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center-head
rubrics_metrics.description: A center-head is a headline placed at equal distances from both margins of the page or column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center-heads are usually set in caps or in small caps, and are not followed by a period. When a center-head runs more than one line, use the inverted 'pyramid' form for two or three lines or 'hanging indention' for more than three lines. (Example: 'SEC. VII. THE PRINCIPLES OF SOCIOLOGY')

rubrics_metrics.name: Side-head
rubrics_metrics.description: A side-head is a headline placed at the side of the page or column.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A side-head may be set in a separate line (usually flush with margin) or run in with the paragraph (more common). Side-heads are most frequently set in italics with only the first word and proper names capitalized; sometimes in caps and small caps or bold face. Example forms given: 'Side-head— A side-head is ...' and variations with punctuation and case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut-in head
rubrics_metrics.description: A cut-in head is a head placed in a box cut into the side of the type-page, usually set in different type, and as a rule placed under the first two lines of the paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distinct type and box placement under the opening lines of the paragraph to visually separate the cut-in head from body text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box-head
rubrics_metrics.description: A box-head is a head for a column in a ruled table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use box-heads for column headings in tabular material (see table rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Running-head
rubrics_metrics.description: A running-head is a headline placed at the top of each page of a book, usually giving the main title on the left (verso) and the chapter or subdivision title on the right (recto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running-heads should be centered on the page regardless of page number. A practical rule: set running-heads in roman or italic capitals two sizes smaller than the text type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph types (plain and hanging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two kinds of paragraphs are distinguished — plain (regular) and hanging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A plain paragraph has the first line indented and the others set flush. A hanging paragraph has the first line set flush and the others indented. Use appropriate form for bibliographic entries and other contexts (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Galley-proof definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A galley-proof is an impression of the type contained in a long, shallow receptacle of metal (a galley) into which material is placed as it is set, line by line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Galley-proofs are early proofs of type composition and should be used for corrections before pagination; keep galley order and identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page-proof definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A page-proof is an impression of the type material made up into page-form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page-proofs reflect pagination and make-up; corrections here may be more expensive because of resetting and repaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plate-proof / Foundry-proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A plate-proof or foundry-proof is a proof taken of the type-page immediately before an electrotype cast is made of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proof often has a black border from the metal frame; many publications print from plates rather than directly from type, so plate proofs are critical — corrections to plates are expensive and likely to injure plates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foul proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A foul proof is a galley-proof containing the author's corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foul proofs combine compositor output with author markups and should accompany later proofs for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise (new corrected proof)
rubrics_metrics.description: A revise is a new proof of type corrected from a marked proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each successive revise should be accompanied by the previous marked set to track changes and charges for alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up
rubrics_metrics.description: The arranging into page-form of type-lines is called the make-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make-up requires attention to pagination, running-heads, folios, and ensuring final product page counts fit printer's forms (even forms of 16, 12, or 8 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Folio and drop-folio
rubrics_metrics.description: A folio is a page-number. Even numbers go on the verso; odd on the recto. A drop-folio is a page-number placed at the bottom of a page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place folios consistently (even=verso, odd=recto); set running-heads centered regardless of folio placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Half-title / Bastard title
rubrics_metrics.description: A half-title or bastard title is the abbreviated title of a book placed on a separate page preceding the full title-page, or the title of a part/chapter placed on a separate page preceding that part/chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit copy for title-pages, prefaces, and tables of contents with the manuscript; index copy should be compiled from special page-proofs furnished for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotype
rubrics_metrics.description: The monotype is a composing-machine where perforated paper strips drive a second machine that casts individual characters and arranges them automatically on a galley in justified lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotype composition casts characters separately; changes to numbers or characters may be simpler than linotype resetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linotype
rubrics_metrics.description: The linotype is a composing-machine where matrices arrange automatically in lines and are cast into slugs (stereotyped strips) of type on the same machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linotype produces slugs (lines) and requires resetting whole lines when small changes are made; this has implications for numbering footnotes and for the cost of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript legibility and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be either typewritten or in a perfectly clear handwriting; typewritten is preferable. Sheets should be of uniform size (9" x 11" desirable) and only one side used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never roll manuscripts; place flat in box/envelope. Use pins or clips only (no permanent fastening). Write proper names, foreign words, and figures with utmost care and distinctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fastening and inserts
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets should not be fastened together except by pins or clips; when one piece of a page is to be fastened to another use mucilage, not pins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pins may become unfastened and cause loss of slips. Additions to original pages should be placed after the sheets to which they belong and marked 'Insert A', etc.; indicate insertion points on margins with 'Here insert A.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberal margins should be left at the top and left-hand side for reader/printer directions. Pages should be numbered consecutively. Inserted and omitted pages should be clearly indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number inserted pages as 4A, 4B; indicate omitted pages by numbering p. 4, '4-7'. This clarity prevents misplacement during make-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph marking in manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs should be plainly indicated either by indenting the first line or by a ^ mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear paragraph demarcation prevents misreading during composition and proofing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnote preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes should be clearly designated (separated by a rule or different ink color); the word in the text carrying the note should be followed by a superior figure corresponding to the note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not run footnotes into the text in manuscripts (not in parentheses or otherwise). Number footnotes consecutively throughout an article or by chapters; bear in mind linotype resetting: changing one number may force resetting of many lines, so number consecutively with caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading timing and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and return proofs promptly. In marking proof-sheets, use the standard proofreaders' marks (do not adopt a system of your own).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer all queries in proofs. Changes in type cost money — make manuscripts as perfect as possible before delivering to the printer. Make necessary alterations in the galley-proof rather than later stages. Corrections in plates should be studiously avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returning manuscripts and proof sets
rubrics_metrics.description: The original manuscript should be returned with the galley-proof so the proofreader may refer to it; each successive set of proofs returned should be accompanied by the previous marked set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This practice assists in calculating costs of alterations and tracing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's professional duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Read everything as if you yourself were the author; verify proper names and figures and check all dates. Do not follow copy blindly — follow only where it is correct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When in doubt, look up facts or query the author. Make queries clear and prominent; be discreet and avoid trivial criticisms. Correct anything palpably wrong even if copy asserts the contrary — the proofreader will bear blame for errors left uncorrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader's relation to authors/editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not ask authors or editors to decide questions of style; the Manual of Style is primarily meant for the proofreader. Do not regard an author's or editor's 'O.K.' as relieving you of responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors depend on proofreaders to ensure typographical requirements and adopted style are met; maintain professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading speed and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivate speed, but accuracy is more important; in unavoidable 'rush' cases, protect yourself by making clear you did your best in the time allotted and disclaim further responsibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If time provided is insufficient, take reasonable extra time to ensure correctness. The long-term credit for accuracy outweighs short-term displeasure about lack of dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing and recording proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the reading, sign all galley- and page-proofs in the upper right-hand corner with your initial above that of the copyholder and reviser; if copyholding and revising are done by different people place initials in prescribed positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark number of proofs wanted on first readings before sending to corrector. Enter date and hour of sending out proofs on the page-slip; record number of pages and plates and total pages of the finished product including preliminaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make-up and final checks by proofreader
rubrics_metrics.description: When reading page-proofs, revise by checking with author's alterations first; then make copy for contents and return to be set so cover and contents may be ready with page-proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read running-heads and folios as a separate operation after finishing page reading. Ensure the finished book/journal will contain even forms (16/12/8 pages) and raise question if not. Number and indicate half-titles, blank pages, inserts, etc., and carry necessary queries on every set of proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyholder conduct and technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyholders should cultivate a low, soft, clear reading voice, enunciate small words and plural s's distinctly, regulate speed, and avoid guessing words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the proofreader time to mark; slow up when the proofreader puts pencil to paper. Develop simple signals (voice raise/tap) to indicate italics etc., to avoid long verbal descriptions. Read all instructions and stet-marks carefully and learn the job number for every galley.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyholder responsibilities for proof sets and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult the job ticket for number of proofs and destination before having proofs corrected. Be careful transferring marks — a mark in the wrong place causes two errors instead of one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy all queries and make-up instructions on the galley-proof; indicate insertion points for tables/figures where first mentioned. The manuscript should accompany the galley-proof; the foul proof should accompany the page-proof if a galley-proof was sent. Indicate envelope contents in lower left corner; fasten pins in center top to avoid covering directions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofroom housekeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyholder is the housekeeper of the proof-room and must keep it neat and orderly so everything can be located at a moment's notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return borrowed volumes and proofs to file daily; return proofs ready for filing at least once a day. Perfect a system for locating material quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standard proofreader's marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use standard proofreader's marks to indicate deletions, insertions, spacing changes, font/style changes, paragraph breaks, indentation, transposition, and queries to author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: 'Dele, or delete: take out.' (dele); 'Letter reversed — turn.'; 'Put in space.'; 'Close up — no space.'; 'Bad spacing — space more evenly.'; 'Wrong font: character of wrong size or style.'; 'Transpose.'; 'Make a new paragraph.'; 'Indent; or, put in an em-quad space.'; 'Carry to the left/right.'; 'Elevate.'; 'Imperfect type — correct.'; 'Space shows between words — push down.'; 'Straighten crooked line.'; 'Restore or return words crossed out.'; 'Print (a f f) as a ligature.'; 'Words are omitted from, or in copy.'; 'Query to author: Is this correct?' ; 'Put in bold face type.' — learn and use these standard marks rather than inventing personal symbols.
